Article Title: Many takers for AI books at Madurai fair, but writers wary
Article Text: Madurai: Amid the controversy over AI-generated books at Madurai’s Kalaignar Centenary Library, the annual book fair being held at Tamukkam Grounds, barely five minutes away, has been seeing enthusiastic buyers for similar books. From colourful comics to children’s novels, titles featuring AI-generated illustrations and stories are attracting young readers, even as writers warn that the trend could threaten original creativity.At several stalls, AI illustrations have found their way into abridged classics, comics, colouring books and children’s stories. Among the attractions is a Robin Hood comic produced entirely using AI. With brighter visuals and lifelike characters, such books are catching the attention of children, while parents say the illustrations appear more realistic than conventional artwork. Many buyers are unaware that the images, and sometimes the stories themselves, are machine-generated.For publishers, however, the attraction goes beyond appearances. Producing illustrations through AI considerably reduces costs, allowing them to offer books at competitive prices. “We use AI to make these books more affordable to the consumer, as they are cheaper to produce as well,” said a publisher selling the Robin Hood comic.He said AI-generated titles were selling as well as conventional comics at his stall with prices ranging from Rs 50 to Rs 600.What excites young readers has left established writers uneasy. Sahitya Akademi award-winning writer S Ramakrishnan said the current enthusiasm for AI could be short-lived, but its impact on literature might be significant. “AI can only duplicate, not create. Those creating new things with their works should have nothing to fear,” he said. Ramakrishnan stressed the need for publishers to disclose how extensively AI was used in producing books, allowing buyers to make informed choices.Echoing his concerns, writer Latshmi Har suggested creating a separate category for AI-assisted books. Both writers maintained that original literary works would continue to find readers despite the technology’s growing influence.Meanwhile, the fair has attracted around 38,000 visitors over the past week, with publishers hoping for stronger sales during the final weekend. Jyothi, who manages a comic book stall, attributed the relatively subdued turnout to the fair being held later than its usual September schedule.
Article Summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being used to create colourful comics and children's novels. Publishers say the technology reduces costs, allowing them to offer books at competitive prices. Writers warn that the trend could threaten original creativity. The annual book fair in Madurai has attracted 38,000 visitors over the past week.

Article Title: In 2002, Kentucky researchers examined 20 treated subgrade sections across 14 road sites; after 8–15 years, treated soil’s CBR ranged from 24 to 59, versus 2 for untreated soil
Article Text:
AI Representation: Kentucky researchers tested 20 treated subgrade sections across 14 road sites. Image credits: Chatgpt

Researchers examined 20 treated road sections

Treated soil recorded a much higher

CBR

value

Most road sections remained in good condition

Findings supported the long-term value of soil stabilisation

Roads in Kentucky. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Roads depend on the soil beneath them to support traffic and prevent pavement damage. When the underlying layer is weak, repeated vehicle loads can contribute to cracking, rutting and surface deterioration. In a 2002 study, researchers at the University of Kentucky examined whether chemical treatments could improve road subgrade strength over the long term. They studied 20 treated sections across 14 sites where the pavements had already been in service for approximately 8 to 15 years. The findings appeared in Long-Term Benefits of Stabilizing Soil Subgrades , published in June 2002 by the Kentucky Transportation Center. Tommy C. Hopkins, Tony L. Beckham, Liecheng Sun, Bixian Ni and Barry Butcher conducted the research. The full report is available through the University of Kentucky’s UKnowledge repository Chemical stabilisation of road subgrades had been used in Kentucky since the mid-1980s to improve foundation strength. The study aimed to find out whether these improvements had lasted after years of traffic and weathering. The researchers studied 20 chemically treated sections at 14 road sites. Scientists took approximately 455 samples of soil cores from both treated soil and non-treated soil beneath it.In the experiments, scientists used several types of chemical stabiliser: hydrated lime, Portland cement, a combination of hydrated lime and Portland cement and a by-product of hydrated lime production known in the study as MKD.One of the tests measured the California Bearing Ratio (CBR), which compares the penetration resistance of the soil with that of standard crushed rock. Engineers use it to judge how well soil can support load under a road and a higher value generally means a stronger subgrade. In terms of CBR at the 85th percentile, chemical treatment of the subgrade resulted in in-situ values of CBR that ranged from 24 to 59. The corresponding value of soil beneath the layer of treated soil was only two. Hence, treated soil gave results that were about 12 to 30 times better than those of untreated soil. A falling weight deflectometer was also used to determine how the pavement behaved under load. Back-calculated modulus values for the treated layers were about twice those of the untreated soil.Additionally, pavement condition status was considered along with soil strength test results. Twelve out of 14 roadways had pavements in good condition, according to Kentucky Transportation Cabinet criteria. The research team projected that these pavements would still be rated good at the end of their 20-year design period. Two roadways had a thin overlay of asphalt pavement after about 15 years. There was a difference in the soil layer condition as well. The untreated subgrade had a soft, moisture-affected surface layer, while the treated soils did not. This contributed to the better engineering characteristics of the chemically stabilised materials.The study offered proof in the field that chemical improvement of road foundations would last through many years of use. The research included data from multiple locations with various stabilisers. This enabled the engineering personnel to evaluate the effectiveness of treatment through the test period rather than short laboratory tests. The research team also developed structural layer coefficients for estimating the load-carrying capacity of pavements built over chemically treated foundations.The values were tested using sections of the roads that were designed with thinner pavement.The research indicated that stabilisation of the road helped in maintaining the structural integrity of the road foundation. This does not imply that all treatments would be equally effective. Main factors such as composition of soil, moisture content, methods of construction and traffic loading have an impact on performance. The study helped transportation departments understand that the benefits of soil stabilization would last long after the construction process. It might also provide the designers of pavement structures with more design options.
Article Summary: Researchers at the University of Kentucky examined whether chemical treatments could improve road subgrade strength over the long term. Chemical stabilisation of road subgrades had been used in Kentucky since the mid-1980s to improve foundation strength. The study aimed to find out whether these improvements had lasted after years of traffic and weathering.

Article Title: Kuala Lumpur built a highway that turns into a flood drain; when storms hit, the cars clear out and the river flows through the same tunnel
Article Text:
AI Representation: Kuala Lumpur built a highway that turns into a flood drain. Image credits: Chatgpt

How the tunnel diverts flood water

Four operating modes control traffic and water flow

Entrance to Kuala Lumpur's SMART tunnel. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

A system designed for a specific flood catchment

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kuala Lumpur has a tunnel that serves two purposes. During normal weather, drivers use it to travel between the city centre and the southern gateway at Sungai Besi. When heavy rain raises river levels, the same underground structure helps divert excess water away from flood-prone parts of the city. Known as the Stormwater Management and Road Tunnel or SMART Tunnel, the system was completed in May 2007, according to MMC Corporation, one of its builders. The Institution of Civil Engineers describes it as the world’s longest multipurpose tunnel.To accommodate floodwater from the Klang and Ampang Rivers, as well as to alleviate traffic on the road towards Sungai Besi, the Malaysian government created the project known as SMART. This included construction of a 9.7 km dedicated flood conveyance tunnel with a 3 km, double-deck highway. The highway extends from the Kampung Pandan area, through to the Kuala Lumpur-Seremban Expressway at TUDM Airfield in Sungai Besi. According to the Department of Irrigation and Drainage Malaysia, the system was designed to manage excess water from the Klang-Ampang catchment.The floodwater route is adjacent to Kampung Berembang, which is located at the juncture of the Klang and Ampang rivers.When river levels are high, most of the excess water is diverted into a holding pond and then through the bypass tunnel before it reaches the attenuation pond in Taman Desa. From there, the water is discharged into the Kerayong River through a dual box culvert.SMART has four operating modes, depending on the levels of rainfall and river conditions. Mode one, which is the normal operating condition, has the motorway fully operational and no diversion of flood water. Mode two begins when flow at the L4 monitoring station is between 70 and 150 cubic metres per second. In this case, water starts to flow through the lower drainage section of the tunnel while traffic continues to use the motorway above. If the flow in the rivers is above 150 cubic metres per second, mode three applies and the motorway is closed and evacuated, which normally takes around an hour. During this time, the water again passes through the lower drainage section of the tunnel, while the motorway decks are kept clear in case mode four is needed. If the storm eases before mode four is needed, the motorway can reopen within 2 to 8 hours of closing, according to the SMART Tunnel’s operational modes.Mode four is used when a major storm continues and the system needs more capacity. After traffic has been evacuated, the motorway compartments are also used to carry floodwater. Authorities generally confirm this mode one or two hours after mode three begins. Once the water has passed, the tunnel remains closed for dewatering, cleaning and inspection. Reopening can take up to four days from the initial closure.A real-time flood detection and forecasting system helps authorities monitor rainfall, river flow and water levels. These readings guide decisions about when to change operating modes and whether traffic must leave the tunnel. The Institution of Civil Engineers identifies MMC Corporation Berhad as the project’s structural engineer and Mott MacDonald as the consulting engineer.The tunnel was built by a joint venture of MMC Corporation Berhad and Gamuda Berhad. Construction lasted about four years and the tunnel opened in 2007. SMART does not eliminate all flood risk in Kuala Lumpur. Its role is limited to water from the Klang-Ampang catchment, so flooding caused by rainfall or reverse flow outside this area cannot be managed through the tunnel. However, it gives the city a way to divert excess water from two major river catchments while keeping an important road connection available during less severe storms.
Article Summary: Kuala Lumpur has a tunnel that serves two purposes. During normal weather, drivers use it to travel between the city centre and the southern gateway. When heavy rain raises river levels, the same structure helps divert excess water away from flood-prone parts of the city.

Article Title: Musk's SpaceXSI denies liability over Grok-generated sexualised images of UK lawmaker

Lawmaker challenges company's defence

A test case for AI companies

Grok faces scrutiny across countries

Elon Musk's SpaceX Super Intelligence (SpaceXSI) has denied legal responsibility for fake sexualised images of a British lawmaker generated using its Grok AI platform. In a written defence filed at London's High Court on October 29, the company argued that AI-generated images that are obviously fictitious cannot violate a person's right to privacy. The response came in a lawsuit filed by Jess Asato, a member of Britain's governing Labour Party, who is seeking an order to prevent Grok from creating manipulated images of her.SpaceXSI has denied allegations of misuse of private information and breaches of data protection laws. It has also contested Asato's request for an order requiring it to "implement effective and permanent technical measures" to stop Grok from generating manipulated images of her.In its defence, lawyers for SpaceX Super Intelligence LLC said the company had removed AI-generated images of Asato that violated its terms. These included a video showing her "being chloroformed and prepared for a sexual assault".However, the company argued that other images it had allowed to remain online were clearly artificial.They said such content "would be understood by reasonable and sensible persons viewing that content to be AI-generated, fictitious and implausible ...rather than as realistic images".On this basis, the company argued that Asato could not claim a reasonable expectation of privacy.SpaceXSI also denied violating her data protection rights. It argued that it "did not determine the content of the relevant users' prompts".Asato hit back at the company's position on Thursday, saying that developers of powerful AI tools must be held accountable for their products."SpaceX SI wants to have it both ways," she said."The company admits it built the AI model, rewrote user requests to add its own graphic details, pulled images from across the internet, and published the results from an account it controls," she said, adding: "Yet it also claims it is a neutral bystander without legal responsibility".Asato has accused the company of designing and training Grok in a way that enabled users to generate sexualised images of her. Her lawsuit alleges misuse of private information and breaches of data protection laws.The lawsuit is among the first cases to examine whether an AI developer can be held legally responsible for the way its system is designed and the content it generates.The court's eventual findings could have implications for similar cases involving AI-generated content and the responsibilities of companies developing such tools.Grok, which is available through Musk's social media platform X, has faced regulatory scrutiny in several countries following an outcry over its use to generate sexualised images of people without their consent.In mid-January, xAI said it had restricted image editing on Grok. It also said it had blocked users from generating images of people in revealing clothing "where it's illegal".However, a Reuters investigation in early February found that Grok continued to generate sexualised images even after the restrictions were introduced. The platform did so even when users explicitly warned that the people depicted had not consented.In July, xAI sued a man in the US, alleging that he had misused Grok to create child sexual abuse material. The case was among the first of its kind brought by an AI company.
Article Summary: Elon Musk's SpaceX Super Intelligence (SpaceXSI) has denied legal responsibility for fake sexualised images of a British lawmaker generated using its Grok AI platform. The company argued that AI-generated images that are obviously fictitious cannot violate a person's right to privacy. The response came in a lawsuit filed by Jess Asato, a member of Britain's governing Labour Party.

Article Title: 'Human': Cambridge’s 'word of the year' is a counterbalance to AI
Article Text:
‘Human’ is Cambridge Dictionary’s word of the year 2026

Why ‘human’

The Cambridge Dictionary has named ‘human’ its Word of the Year for 2026, reflecting a growing debate over what distinguishes people from artificial intelligence (AI) as machines become increasingly capable of performing tasks once considered uniquely human.The choice highlights how the rapid spread of AI has prompted people to reconsider the value of human creativity, judgement, emotion and connection. It also points to a change in the way the word is being used, with expressions such as ‘human-written’, ‘human-generated’ and ‘human-made’ increasingly distinguishing work produced by people from content created by AI.Cambridge Dictionary defines ‘human’ as having the qualities, faults and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals or machines.Cambridge Dictionary said the growing presence of AI in everyday life had led to a renewed appreciation of the human element in what people consume and experience.Colin McIntosh, chief editor of Cambridge Dictionary, said: “Artificial intelligence has been a growing presence in society for years now, but this year it seemed to be everywhere. In many areas of life this has led to a re-evaluation of what it means to be human, as a counterbalance to AI.”He added that 2026 had been marked by a renewed appreciation of the human factor and a greater value being placed on human involvement in everyday life. The dictionary said its analysis of language data, internet trends and search habits supported the selection.One of the clearest signs of this shift is the growing use of the word ‘human’ to identify the origin of creative work. As AI-generated writing, images, music and videos become more common, businesses and creators are increasingly highlighting when something has been made by a person.Cambridge described this as a ‘human premium’, the added value people may attach to a product or experience because they know it involved human effort, judgement and craftsmanship. In a marketplace increasingly filled with AI-generated material, the imperfections and personal involvement associated with human work can become part of its appeal.‘Human’ was selected from a shortlist that included ‘agent’, ‘analogue’, ‘wholesome’ and ‘chic’.
Article Summary: Cambridge Dictionary says rapid spread of AI has prompted people to reconsider the value of human creativity, judgement, emotion and connection. ‘Human’ was selected from a shortlist that included ‘agent’, ‘analogue’ and ‘wholesome’

At eight, most children are still figuring out how to use technology for schoolwork and entertainment. Abigail Watt, however, has already begun creating things with it. The young student has developed three artificial intelligence applications, including a 3D explorer and an online book community for children, and taken her interest a step further by teaching all 30 of her classmates how to use AI creatively. Her work has now earned her recognition at the 2026 Overt STEM Awards in Milton Keynes, where she became the youngest finalist and winner in the school's category.As per a report by Business MK, Abigail won the Future Force in STEM award in the school-age category at the ceremony held at Unity Place on November 3. Her projects stood out among entries from a field of more than 50 finalists, which included young innovators, researchers, educators and established organisations working across science, technology, engineering and mathematics.Abigail's three applications are a 3D Explorer Map, an Art App and Page Pals, an online book community designed specifically for children. While the names offer a glimpse into the range of her interests, the projects also demonstrate how she is exploring different ways of using AI, from interactive exploration and creativity to encouraging children to engage with books. The third project, Page Pals, is particularly interesting because it brings technology into the world of children's reading.Rather than treating AI only as a tool for completing tasks, the idea of a book community gives young readers a digital space centred on their interest in stories and books.Her other projects reflect a similar willingness to experiment. The 3D Explorer Map points towards an interest in interactive digital experiences, while the Art App explores the creative possibilities of technology. Together, the three applications earned her recognition from the Overt STEM Awards, which celebrate contributions to science, technology, engineering and mathematics across the Oxford–Cambridge Growth Corridor.Her school, Caroline Haslett Primary School, announced the achievement on November 6, describing Abigail, identified in its announcement as Abigail W (Joules), as the youngest finalist and winner in the awards' history. The school said she had impressed the judges with her three applications and her dedication to sharing AI knowledge with her classmates. It also noted that she faced competition from older finalists, including an A-level student presenting medical devices and AI research.The recognition places Abigail among a wider group of people and organisations whose work was celebrated at this year's awards. The event brought together more than 50 finalists from across the Oxford–Cambridge Growth Corridor, a region spanning areas between Oxford and Cambridge that has become an important centre for research, education, technology and innovation.The awards covered a broad range of achievements. At the University of Buckingham, Jean D'Amour Kwizera received the AI Impact award for developing a system that uses smartphone images, computer vision, object detection and machine learning to help identify counterfeit medicines. Nathan Luccarini of The Bedford College Group won the Future Force in STEM award in the further and higher education category for developing an esports qualification and digital learning pathways. His colleague Duncan Laughton was recognised for moving from engineering into teaching and helping learners build confidence in mathematics.Other winners included STEM On Track, an educational programme that uses go-kart design and racing to introduce students to engineering, physics and teamwork. It received both the STEM Enrichment Initiative award and the overall STEM Champion title. The programme has reached more than 2,400 students across over 140 school teams.The awards also recognised people working to make STEM careers more accessible. Natalie Desty, founder of STEM Returners, received the Women in STEM Champion award, while Pearl Oguchi, founder of the Black Women in Tech community, received the Lifetime Impact in STEM award for her 22-year contribution to technology.The Overt STEM Awards were organised by Events Together and expanded the reach of the earlier MK STEM Awards to recognise talent across the Oxford–Cambridge Growth Corridor. Its categories span school-age projects, higher education, research, industry innovation, mentoring and inclusion. The Future Force in STEM school-age category is intended to showcase young learners between five and 18 who are making an impact through STEM projects.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Article Title: Instagram tests 90-minute horizontal videos - what it means for long-form content creators
Article Text:

Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians, with select creators in the US.The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos, as per The Hollywood Reporter.“What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” vice-president of product at Instagram, Tessa Lyons, said.Instagram has already been testing Features with creators in Brazil and plans to expand the trial to tens of thousands of creators in the US. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.The feature will be available on mobile, with Instagram aiming to extend the viewing experience to its TV app. Instagram for TV, which launched last year and is available on Samsung , Fire TV and Google TV, is now expanding to Apple TV in the US.“We think the best viewing experience for longform horizontal content is on a big, horizontal screen, and so I think that is where we will expect a lot of the deep consumption to happen over time,” Lyons said, as per The Hollywood Reporter.Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile. The move comes amid growing interest in microdramas and episodic videos among creators.In June, the company began reaching out to microdrama studios in Southeast Asia to test the feature. It has since approached individual creators who have been experimenting with episodic content.Instagram plans to begin testing Series in more countries in the coming months, with a US launch targeted for the end of this year or early next year. The company has also started testing how the feature will appear on television.Other experiments include integrating live videos into the Reels tab and recommending them to users who do not follow the creators. The test is launching in Indonesia and Brazil, with an expansion to the US planned for next year.
Article Summary: Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians. Article Text:
As Florida uses robot rabbits to eliminate growing population of Burmese pythons; study reveals when and how these python use trees

Why smaller Burmese pythons climb trees more often

How Florida's robot rabbits help detect Burmese pythons

How many Burmese pythons have been removed in Florida

In 2025, Florida introduced solar-powered robot rabbits to tackle its growing population of invasive Burmese pythons. Now, a new study has revealed when and how these snakes climb trees, giving wildlife officials another clue to help locate and remove them. Researchers tracked 346 Burmese pythons, including 188 adults and 158 juveniles, in Big Cypress National Preserve between 2017 and 2024. According to the US Geological Survey (USGS), the study recorded more than 4,000 habitat data points to understand how the snakes use their surroundings.The findings showed that Burmese pythons mostly stay on the ground, with less than 3% of all sightings involving tree climbing. However, around 17% of juvenile pythons and 14% of adult pythons were spotted climbing trees at least once during the study.Researchers found that juvenile pythons were more likely to climb trees than adults. Their smaller size and lighter weight may make it easier for them to move along branches. As a python grows heavier, its likelihood of climbing trees decreases. This means wildlife workers may need to look beyond the ground when searching for smaller invasive snakes.The findings could help improve python removal efforts because the snakes are already difficult to spot in Florida's dense vegetation.In 2025, the South Florida Water Management District and the University of Florida introduced solar-powered robotic rabbit decoys to attract Burmese pythons. The robots mimic real prey by producing a heat signature and emitting a scent designed to attract snakes. They are also equipped with AI-powered cameras that monitor the surrounding area and alert officials when a python approaches. A trained removal agent can then be sent to capture the snake.“These innovative robots produce a heat signature and emit a smell designed to attract pythons. The robots are equipped with cameras that monitor for pythons and notify District officials when a snake is detected. Once notified, the District can dispatch a python removal agent to the area,” the district said.Burmese pythons are not native to Florida and are found in and around the Everglades, where they prey on birds, mammals and other reptiles, according to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC). Florida also organises the annual Florida Python Challenge, a 10-day competition that brings together professional and amateur hunters to capture the invasive snakes. In the 2026 challenge, 907 participants from 30 states, as well as Vietnam and Canada, removed 280 Burmese pythons.Since 2017, contractors working with the FWC and South Florida Water Management District have removed more than 19,000 snakes.The latest study adds to these efforts by showing that although most Burmese pythons remain on the ground, smaller snakes are more likely to climb trees.
Article Summary: Researchers tracked 346 Burmese pythons, including 188 adults and 158 juveniles, in Big Cypress National Preserve between 2017 and 2024. The study recorded more than 4,000 habitat data points to understand how the snakes use their surroundings. The findings could help improve python removal efforts because the snakes are already difficult to spot in Florida.

Article Title: AI just cracked math’s most famous problem, says Anthropic mathematician; here’s how Google CEO Sundar Pichai reacted

CEO of Anthropic Dario Amodei.

A 167-year-old problem

Claude helped generate a massive proof

Google CEO Sundar Pichai’s reaction

The timing

Just days after Dario Amodei-led Anthropic made its historic public market debut, one of the company's mathematicians has made an even more extraordinary claim: that he has solved the Riemann Hypothesis, widely regarded as the most famous unsolved problem in mathematics, with the help of Anthropic's AI model Claude. According to a Wall Street Journal report cited by the user, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge said he believes he has discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, a landmark conjecture in number theory that has resisted attempts by mathematicians since it was first proposed in 1859.Proposed in 1859, the Riemann hypothesis has defeated the best human minds ever since. It became known as the field’s holy grail when it was chosen as one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems in 2000, and even the most capable AI models hadn’t managed it. Alpöge posted his proof on his website in Lean, a programming language that lets computers check an argument line by line. Mathematicians immediately began working through it. He said the full argument is “incredibly long” and called the AI-written version “some massive unreadable travesty,” more than 250,000 pages.Alpöge revealed that the proof was developed with assistance from Claude, Anthropic's AI system.He published the work in Lean, a programming language and proof assistant designed to allow computers to verify mathematical arguments line by line. According to Alpöge, the complete proof is extraordinarily lengthy. He described the AI-generated version as an "incredibly long" argument spanning more than 250,000 pages. Mathematicians began reviewing the proof soon after it was published, attempting to verify whether the reasoning holds up under scrutiny. Importantly, the proof has not yet been formally accepted by the mathematical community. Independent verification will be required before the result can be considered proven.The announcement quickly drew attention across the technology industry, including from Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet. Reacting to the claim on X, Pichai wrote: "Somewhere Euler, Gauss and Riemann in awe today!" The remark referenced three of the most influential figures in mathematical history: Leonhard Euler, Carl Friedrich Gauss and Bernhard Riemann, whose work laid the foundations for large parts of modern mathematics.Alpöge said the result came late Sunday into Monday, days before Anthropic went public. He called the timing “horrible” and said he messaged CEO Dario Amodei to ask permission to announce it, noting there was a constraint to respect. Anthropic didn’t respond to a request for comment after his post, as its stock fell 13.04% on its first full day of trading.“I just could not live if I waited even longer,” he wrote. He added that he hoped the argument offers “a glimpse towards the miracles that lie ahead.”
Article Summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he has discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. The conjecture is a landmark conjecture in number theory that has resisted attempts by mathematicians since it was first proposed in 1859. The proof was developed with assistance from Anthropic's AI system Claude.

Article Title: ‘Let Students Search’: Google employees want an AI-free option for schools, here’s why

Can schools turn off AI inside Search

Hundreds of Google employees have signed a petition asking the company to give schools a version of Google Search without generative AI. The appeal comes as three of the largest US school districts weigh switching search engines, according to The New York Times. He said students attempting to use Search at schools that ban AI would see a message saying the service was unavailable. Some districts, including New York City, have already restricted student-facing generative AI over concerns about how it affects learning.New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Google of using its market power to push AI into public schools. The union argues that educators should decide when students use AI and that taking away Search could prompt districts to drop other Google products.It also warned that losing school district business could affect job security.“The decision of how and when to implement AI into a classroom belongs to the educators leading it,” Parul Koul, the union’s president and a Google software engineer, said in a statement.Google has said that under changes expected early next year, schools will be able to enable or disable Search, Gemini and NotebookLM individually. That means a school could switch off the standalone Gemini chatbot and keep Search available to students. Google’s clarification left open whether schools could also disable the generative AI features that appear within Search itself.The union said some coverage had made it sound as though Google was deliberately punishing schools for opting out of AI. Its petition asks for a setting that would let schools apply their classroom AI policies to Search while keeping the search engine available for everyday use.

A Meta employee was chatting with Muse about weather and tides when the AI agent brought up two bank balances. It named Capital One and Charles Schwab and gave amounts down to the cent. It remains unclear whether they belonged to someone else or were generated by the AI. The Signal reminder also leaves open how Muse came up with the prompt.That distinction matters because a chat filled with somebody else’s information and a chat filled with invented details can look similar to the person reading it. The employee who asked about the weather had little to go on when Muse switched topics and presented the numbers as a personal update.A Meta spokesperson told TechCrunch that employee testing helps the company gather feedback, build safety and privacy protections and improve its products. The spokesperson also said staff have access to different versions of Muse and often test features and behaviour that people using the public app don’t encounter.The employee accounts describe what happened in those internal tests. The examples reported by Reuters show how ordinary the conversations can be before something unexpected turns up. The employee in the banking example had asked about weather and tides. Article Title: Microsoft 365 outage: Company blames a 'triple' failure for 24-hour-plus global Outlook disruption; Microsoft EVP Charles Lamanna says: Three main factors that...
Article Text:
Microsoft explains its global outage

A July bug slipped past Microsoft 365's load testing

A Teams failover and 14% missing capacity exposed the bug

Outlook stayed down longest because Exchange Online could not switch gateways

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Microsoft has explained what disrupted Outlook, Exchange Online and a string of other Microsoft 365 services for more than 24 hours last week, and the answer is not one fault but three. A software bug that had sat unnoticed on its servers since July, a sudden rise in traffic and a chunk of server capacity already offline all lined up on November 12. The result was a chain reaction that left more than 80% of the servers behind a key Microsoft 365 networking gateway unresponsive at the worst point.Charles Lamanna, Microsoft's executive vice president for Copilot, Agents and Platform, detailed the root cause of the Microsoft 365 outage in a post on X on Monday. "The incident on Thursday, November 12th, 2026, was caused by three main factors that together caused a global outage for the networking gateway that fronts many Microsoft 365 services," he wrote. He also apologised: "We are deeply sorry for the impact to all our customers and recognize the impact that this has on their normal business & operations. "The first factor was a latent defect. Under certain load conditions, lock contention inside an internal process left servers overwhelmed and unresponsive.The bug came from a fix built specifically for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers. Lamanna said neither the defect nor that fix applies to broader Windows deployments.The change began rolling out in July, cleared safe deployment, reached servers worldwide over several weeks and ran for more than three months without trouble.So why did testing miss it? Microsoft's load tests leaned on its weaker hardware with fewer cores, while the contention problem gets worse on newer machines with more cores. The test labs' traffic and hardware mix did not match the live fleet.Microsoft runs two independent network gateway systems inside Microsoft 365, so services can move between them during disruptions. About 15 hours before the outage, Teams failed over from the alternative gateway to the "primary" one, which also handles Exchange Online. The company calls this routine, but it added load and changed traffic patterns on that gateway.At the same time, nearly 14% of the gateway's server capacity was out of service because of an unrelated issue from the day before. That alone caused no harm, since the service had enough headroom.Together, though, the extra load and thinner capacity triggered the July bug during peak US traffic hours. Requests piled up until servers stopped responding. Microsoft's traffic management then moved users to healthy endpoints, as designed, which simply spread the same load across fewer machines. In under two hours, the defect had hit servers across the fleet.A separate issue meant the bulkheads between regional "capacity units" also failed to contain the damage, letting a gateway problem become a global outage.Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint and Office apps could move off the faulty infrastructure, which is why they came back sooner. Teams chats and meetings worked for most of the outage. Exchange Online, which powers Outlook email, could not make that switch.Recovery was a fight of its own. Servers returning to service were flooded by queued traffic and went down again. Microsoft's automated recovery systems were not designed for such a broad failure, and because the bug was months old, the usual rollback, flighting and feature flag tools could not quickly reverse it. Even the company's status updates during the outage said it had "not identified any recent change correlated with the start of impact.Engineers eventually built an update that returned the code path to its last known good state. They then pulled groups of servers out of service, applied the fix and restarted them, in some cases more than half a region at a time.Microsoft first flagged the problem at 11:24 pm IST on November 12, for users in the Americas, before it spread to at least 70 countries and hit Copilot, government offices, courts and hospitals. In India, IndiGo and Akasa Air reported problems with their customer-support email systems, while OpenAI and Anthropic flagged issues with their Microsoft 365 integrations. The Microsoft executive had already ruled out foul play on November 13, writing, "This was not a cyberattack or an issue caused by AI tooling. "A final Post-Incident Review (PIR) is due later this week. It should also shed light on the separate issue that let the failure jump across regions, which Monday's summary leaves unexplained.
Article Summary: Microsoft 365 went down for more than 24 hours on November 12. A software bug that had sat unnoticed on its servers since July, a sudden rise in traffic and a chunk of server capacity already offline all lined up. The result was a chain reaction that left more than 80% of the servers behind a key Microsoft 365 networking gateway unresponsive.

Article Title: Why this WhatsApp rival is blocking screenshots to keep Apple, Google out of your chats
Article Text:
Signal is turning off screenshots on iPhone and Android, and AI is the reason

End-to-end encryption does not cover what Siri AI and Gemini read off your screen

Meta ’s Muse AI agent has already reached into Signal chats through accessibility settings

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support Signal's decision to block screenshots to protect user privacy? Yes, privacy is paramount No, this limits functionality 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Signal will now stop you from taking screenshots inside its app on iPhones and Android phones, and you are not the one it is worried about. The privacy-focused WhatsApp rival says the block is meant to keep AI assistants such as Apple ’s Siri AI and Google ’s Gemini from reading your private chats straight off the screen. The protection is switched on by default on iOS 27, and on Android versions where Signal can detect an AI assistant trying to scan the display. Anyone who wants screenshots back can turn it off in settings, though Signal warns this exposes their chats, and their contacts’, to these agents.In a blog post on November 20, Signal president Meredith Whittaker said AI features built into phone operating systems are weakening the app’s ability to guarantee privacy on its own. She called this deep integration of agents “an existential threat to Signal”.On iPhones, the new toggle appears in Signal’s settings as Block Siri AI. On Android, the app turns on its existing Screen security option when it spots an assistant trying to read the screen. Users also get a pop-up offering to lift the block.Signal’s encryption protects messages as they travel between phones. It cannot do much once an assistant scans an open chat.According to Signal, that captured content can then sit in a local database or move to whichever server the agent relies on, well outside the app’s control. The company says it spent months running forensic checks on Android and iOS to learn what these systems do with app data.Signal admits the fix is incomplete. Blocking screenshots does nothing to stop agents from pulling data stored on the phone through the file system. It also cannot offer the same protection on macOS, since operating system makers give developers no easy way to restrict AI access without hurting how an app works.Signal also flagged third-party agents such as Meta’s Muse, which it says lean on deep accessibility permissions users grant during setup. Reuters reported earlier this week that Muse pulled Signal messages on a Mac and on an Android phone this way. On the Mac, it combined accessibility and screenshot tools to capture the chats and extract the text. An Apple update this week closed that specific route. Meta has said Muse can access other apps only through permissions users explicitly grant.Signal has done this before. Last year, it used the same screenshot block on Windows 11 to keep Microsoft’s Recall feature from saving its chats.Signal, run by the non-profit Signal Technology Foundation, is now asking Apple, Google and Microsoft for two things. The first is a simple, documented way for developers to opt their apps out of AI access, covering screen reading, file access, notifications and other system tools. The second is clear documentation on how these AI agents access and process data. Signal says Google and Apple have begun talking to it about how their AI systems should work with privacy-focused apps.
Article Summary: Signal will now stop you from taking screenshots inside its app on iPhones and Android phones. The privacy-focused WhatsApp rival says the block is meant to keep AI assistants such as Apple ’s Siri AI and Google’s Gemini from reading your private chats straight off the screen. Anyone who wants screenshots back can turn it off in settings.

Article Title: Days after Sundar Pichai congratulated Elon Musk’s space company, Google picks SpaceX-rival to launch AI computing satellites in 2029
Article Text:
Tech giants looking to move power-hungry AI data centers beyond Earth

In-house AI hardware:

Near-continuous sunlight:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jeff Bezos’s space venture Blue Origin and Alphabet’s Google have partnered with the latter has chosen the New Glenn rocket to carry satellites into orbit for Project Suncatcher, an initiative designed to run artificial intelligence (AI) systems in space. Scheduled for the first quarter of 2029, the mission will serve as Google’s first heavy-lift flight dedicated to Project Suncatcher, sending multiple computing satellites aboard New Glenn. The agreement also hands Blue Origin a high-profile future contract for New Glenn as the company works to grow its launch business following earlier delays and a launchpad explosion in May.The partnership announcement comes days after Google CEO Sundar Pichai congratulated SpaceX and its CEO Elon Musk after the company achieved its first-ever midair catch of a Starship spacecraft – a reusable upper-stage spacecraft and super heavy-lift launch system – returning from space. Pichai said the achievement “still feels like science fiction” and added that watching the event live was incredible.As surging AI adoption drives up demand for computing power and strains terrestrial electricity grids, land and cooling systems, tech and space companies, including Elon Musk’s SpaceX and startup Starcloud, are exploring orbital data centers as an alternative. Google’s upcoming mission aims to test whether continuous solar power in space can support heavy AI workloads:Each satellite will be equipped with Google’s tensor processing units (TPUs), custom chips engineered to run AI models, packing roughly the computing capacity of a full server rack in a traditional ground-based data center.The spacecraft will be placed into an orbit that will have near-constant sunlight to evaluate how effectively solar energy can power sustained computing off-planet.Notably, the efforts are built on an earlier SpaceX prototype flight. In October, Google and Planet Labs launched the first Project Suncatcher prototype aboard a SpaceX rocket, later confirming the satellite was functioning as expected after making contact.The 2029 Blue Origin mission builds on groundwork already underway.That initial test flight is examining how Google’s chips hold up against intense launch forces, space radiation, and extreme temperature swings, while helping engineers figure out how to manage heat without Earth’s natural airflow.Meanwhile, engineering and cost challenges remain. For example, space radiation can degrade electronics and corrupt data, while heat generated by high-powered chips must be dissipated using specialised pipes and panels instead of standard cooling fans or liquid systems.Industry experts have pointed out that steep launch expenses, complex engineering demands and limited satellite manufacturing capacity mean commercial orbital data centers are likely still years away.
Article Summary: Project Suncatcher aims to test whether continuous solar power in space can support heavy AI workloads. Each satellite will be equipped with Google’s tensor processing units (TPUs), custom chips engineered to run AI models. The spacecraft will be placed into an orbit that will have near-constant sunlight.

What should students and alumni check

Microsoft is phasing out free student and alumni email service. The company says it will retire Office 365 A1, the Student Use Benefit program and its free Exchange Online for Alumni offer on January 1, 2028. Schools, colleges and universities with an active enrollment that began before that date can keep using those licenses until the end of their current term.For students who receive coursework and campus notices at a school address, and graduates who still use a university inbox, the timing depends on when their institution’s agreement ends. Schools that want to keep those Microsoft-hosted mailboxes will need to move users to an eligible paid license. Institutions that switch email providers will need to tell users how and when to access their mail.Office 365 A1 will first reach the end of sale through Microsoft’s partner channels on May 1, 2027. Institutions with a qualifying active enrollment can still add A1 licenses during their existing term. This means a school can continue assigning accounts under that enrollment while it decides how to handle email once the agreement ends.Microsoft’s new education lineup includes a no-cost student plan called Microsoft 365 Education A0. It includes desktop and web versions of Office apps for eligible students. Exchange Online, the service that hosts Microsoft school mailboxes, is available on paid student plans starting with Microsoft 365 Education A2.Microsoft says institutions can assign different licenses to different user groups. A university could buy licenses for students who need Microsoft-hosted email and use the no-cost plan for eligible students whose email is handled by another provider.Microsoft will offer a paid version of Exchange Online for Alumni. Universities that choose to continue providing Microsoft-hosted email to graduates can move them to the paid offer after their current term. Whether a graduate keeps the same address will depend on what the university decides to provide.Students and alumni can ask their institution’s IT department when their current email service is due to change and whether the school plans to keep their address active. If the institution is moving to another provider, users can check whether existing messages and contacts will be transferred and how long they will have access to the old inbox.Graduates who use a university address for job applications, professional contacts or personal accounts may need to update those records if their address is being retired. The same applies to services that send password reset links or verification codes to a school inbox. Those details are easier to change while the account can still receive mail.

Article Title: Samsung co-CEO TM Roh steps down as mobile chief to focus on robotics, Galaxy S26 lead Won-Joon Choi takes over
Article Text:
The logo of the Samsung Electronics Co. is seen at its office in Seoul, South Korea, Wednesday, May 20, 2026. (AP Photo/Ahn Young-joon)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Samsung Electronics has a new boss for its smartphone business. Co-CEO TM Roh is stepping down as head of the Mobile eXperience (MX) business and handing the role to Won-Joon Choi, who led development of the Galaxy S26 and Galaxy Z Fold8 series.The change is part of Samsung ’s 2027 leadership reshuffle, announced on November 20. Roh isn’t going anywhere, though. He stays on as co-CEO and head of the Device eXperience (DX) division, and will now also focus on the company’s Robotics eXperience office. The idea, Samsung says, is to speed up new businesses like robotics.DX is the Samsung arm behind Galaxy phones, TVs and home appliances, while the Device Solutions (DS) division runs the chip business.Choi has been chief operating officer of MX since March 2025, so the phone business stays with someone who knows it from the inside. Under him, Samsung is expected to sharpen its focus on foldables, on-device AI and wearables.The bigger shake-up is on the semiconductor side, where three chip veterans have been promoted to president.Sang Joon Hwang, who led memory development across DRAM and high bandwidth memory (HBM), now heads the Memory business.Sangyeun Cho, who previously ran Samsung’s chip operations in the US, takes over System LSI, the unit that designs Exynos processors and camera sensors. Samsung is counting on his ties with global customers to win new clients.Jong Myeong Lee, a process engineer with about 28 years of experience across DRAM, NAND and foundry, becomes chief technology officer of DS and head of the semiconductor R&D centre.Vice Chairman Young Hyun Jun continues as co-CEO and head of DS. Now that Hwang is in charge of memory, Jun gives up his extra role as memory chief to concentrate on foundry and other future chip businesses.In all, six executives were named. Samsung says appointments at the vice president level and below, along with further organisational changes, will follow soon.
Article Summary: Co-CEO TM Roh is stepping down as head of the Mobile eXperience (MX) business. Won-Joon Choi, who led development of the Galaxy S26 and Galaxy Z Fold8 series, will take over. Roh isn’t going anywhere, though, and will now focus on the company’s Robotics experience office.

Article Title: GTA 6 PC scam alert: $200 malware kit targets gamers with fake downloads and crypto theft
Article Text:
A still from GTA 6. Image via: Rockstar Games

GTA 6 PC scam kit uses fake downloads to steal sensitive data

How to spot a fake GTA 6 download and protect your computer

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

GTA 6 fans waiting for a PC release have become targets of a dangerous online scam. Cybersecurity researchers have uncovered a $200 malware package that uses fake game downloads to trick players into infecting their computers. The toolkit reportedly combines account-stealing software, cryptocurrency theft tools and hidden mining programmes. With Rockstar Games yet to announce a native PC version, the promise of an unofficial download could cost players far more than they expect. The threat also reaches beyond gaming, potentially putting personal email, financial accounts and workplace information at risk.NordVPN’s Threat Intelligence team discovered the toolkit on November 16, three days before GTA 6 launched on consoles. According to the findings, the package was advertised on the dark web for $200, with buyers able to pay using Bitcoin or Tether.The toolkit reportedly includes several malicious programmes. One executable, named GTA6 Keygen.exe, is designed to capture browser session cookies. These files help websites keep users signed in. If criminals steal them, they may be able to access accounts without entering passwords or completing another two-factor authentication check.The package also contains a cryptocurrency wallet drainer targeting networks such as Ethereum, Solana, Polygon and BNB Smart Chain. Another component uses XMRig software to mine cryptocurrency secretly by consuming the victim’s computer resources.It even includes an automated YouTube Shorts tool that can promote fraudulent download links. This could help scammers reach more gamers through videos that appear connected to GTA 6.Rockstar has released the game for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, but has not announced a native PC version. Official cloud streaming on supported Xbox devices does not provide an installable PC copy.A website claiming to offer a free GTA 6 PC installer should raise immediate suspicion. Other warning signs include unofficial game ports, key generators, cracked files and links shared through unfamiliar social media accounts. Players should also avoid downloads that ask them to disable antivirus protection or connect a crypto wallet to unlock access.If you have downloaded a suspicious file but have not opened it, delete it and run a security scan. If you have already executed it, disconnect the computer from the internet and scan it with updated security software.Use a separate, trusted device to change important passwords, especially for email and banking accounts. Also sign out of active sessions, revoke unfamiliar devices and check financial and crypto accounts for unusual activity. If the computer connects to workplace systems, inform the organisation’s IT team.The discovery follows an earlier campaign involving fake GTA 6 demo websites that distributed Vidar malware. The latest findings suggest scammers are now packaging several harmful tools into one product. Until Rockstar announces an official PC release, players should treat any downloadable GTA 6 installer as a potential threat.
Article Summary: GTA 6 PC scam kit uses fake downloads to steal sensitive data. Toolkit reportedly combines account-stealing software, cryptocurrency theft tools and hidden mining programmes. With Rockstar Games yet to announce a native PC version, the promise of an unofficial download could cost players far more than they expect.

Article Title: GTA 6 graphics settings on Xbox: How to get the best visual experience
Article Text:
Best settings that you can use for GTA 6 (Image via Rockstar Games)

GTA 6 Xbox settings guide

Setting Xbox Series X Xbox Series S Resolution 4K UHD (based on your display)t 1080p HDR On On VRR On On TV Motion Smoothing Off Off HGiG On On Audio Toggle on 360 Spatial Sound Toggle on 360 Spatial Sound

Resolution

GTA 6 supports 4K on the Series X, which makes it the better way to play on that console. If you have a 4K display, set your Xbox output to 4K UHD. On the Series S, stick with 1080p. The smaller console is unlikely to handle 4K well, and a lower resolution should give you a better experience.

HDR

HDR is supported, so turn on HDR10 on both consoles if your TV or monitor can handle it. If your display doesn't support HDR, leave it off, since a mismatch can wash out colors. Where available, enable HGiG as well. It helps your console and display coordinate brightness so highlights aren't clipped.

Refresh rate and VRR

GTA 6 is locked at 30 FPS on both Series X and Series S. A display with a higher refresh rate won't change that, but Variable Refresh Rate still helps. With VRR turned on, your screen adjusts its refresh rate to match the game's frame rate, which reduces tearing and judder. If VRR isn't available, you can instead lock your refresh rate to 30 Hz, which can make motion feel smoother.

TV settings

Turn off TV Motion Smoothing. This feature adds artificial frames, which can introduce input lag and give the game an unnatural, soap-opera look. Most TVs have a Game Mode that disables this processing automatically, so that's worth using too.

Audio

The game's soundtrack is a big part of its atmosphere, so audio matters. If your setup supports it, enable 360 Spatial Sound , and use headphones for the best effect. It makes Vice City's radio and street ambience feel more immersive.

Quick checklist

Set your output resolution to 4K (Series X) or 1080p (Series S). Turn on HDR10 and HGiG if your display supports them. Enable VRR. Switch off TV Motion Smoothing, or use Game Mode. Turn on 360 Spatial Sound.
